analysis.title: Global Economics Weekly: Turbulent, not terrible
key_insights: October US CPI beat expectations for a third straight month: headline +0.35% m/m (Barclays 0.24%, consensus 0.3%), core +0.30% m/m (Barclays 0.22%, consensus 0.2%). Core CPI runs 3.7% on a 3m saar basis and 2.7% on a 6m saar basis.

Core goods drove the upside (+0.16% m/m) through freight and energy pass-through and AI-related electronics costs. Core services rose 0.34% m/m. Used cars subtracted about 4bp from core CPI. PPI shows firming pipeline pressure in core goods.

Barclays translates the CPI and PPI into October core PCE of 0.29% m/m (3.2% y/y). It raised its Q4/Q4 2026 core PCE forecast by 0.1pp to 3.3%, conditioned on core CPI slowing to about 0.24% m/m in November and December.

Barclays keeps its call for 25bp Fed hikes in December and January 2027, taking the funds rate to 4.25-4.50%. It then expects a hold until late 2028 and one cut late in 2028. It sees risks to the path skewed to the upside.

Governor Waller backed a December hike regardless of data and floated 50bp if core CPI printed around 0.3% m/m. Barclays doubts a jumbo hike gains traction. Hammack declined to endorse 50bp, and Goolsbee, Williams, Schmid, Daly and Collins all wanted more tightening but without Waller's urgency.

Markets now fully price a December Fed hike with an 11% chance of 50bp. ECB December hike pricing is 95%, up from 78% a week earlier. The 10y Treasury yield rose over 25bp on the week and the 10y Bund over 10bp.

ECB's Lane called a December hike prudent if the information set is unchanged, and Nagel called it rather obvious. Barclays expects a final 25bp hike in December (deposit rate 2.75%), with risk of another in Q1 2027 if energy prices fail to normalise.

Oil eased on signs of reduced US appetite for renewed strikes on Iran. Brent briefly fell below $90/bbl for the first time since August, then rose to about $96 after Trump said a deal was not needed. Barclays sees no final Iran deal soon, keeping oil below pre-midterm highs but well above pre-war levels.

European gas storage is about 70%, well below historical levels, which limits downside in TTF (below EUR90/MWh). Middle East oil flows are about 85% of pre-war levels while inventories remain depressed.
Equities rebounded this week with the Nasdaq 100 up about 5% after a rough post-midterm stretch. Nvidia's governance scrutiny and its earnings next week are flagged as the key test for the AI trade.

Barclays global growth forecast for 2026 is 3.4% (+0.1pp vs September) and 3.2% for 2027 (unchanged). US 2026 growth is 2.4% (+0.3pp), euro area 1.1%, UK 1.6%, Japan 0.9% (-0.2pp). AI investment is a major support in Emerging Asia, especially Taiwan (13.0%) and Korea (3.8%).

US outlook extended to 2028: GDP slows from 2.5% Q4/Q4 in 2026 to 2.0% in 2027 and 1.75% in 2028 as the fiscal tailwind turns to a drag and AI capex contribution falls from about 1.0pp to 0.7pp then 0.2pp. Core PCE falls to 2.6% at end-2027 and 2.2% at end-2028.

SF Fed estimates attribute about 1.4pp of Q3 productivity growth (2.1% 4q) to utilisation, leaving structural productivity at 0.6%. Barclays expects a utilisation unwind to lift unit labor costs and mask productivity gains.
Rent disinflation and memory-chip cost pass-through into electronics are cited as two structural disinflation sources that have weakened, implying slower core progress.

Euro area growth is forecast at 1.1% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2027 and 2028. Headline inflation stays near 4% in coming months and returns to target only in Q1 2028. France is the weak link, with growth of 0.3% in 2026 and elections on 18 April and 2 May 2027.

UK: Q3 GDP +0.7% q/q in line, September +0.2% m/m. Barclays sees CPI peaking at 4.1% in January, unemployment rising to 5.6% by mid-2027, one more 25bp BoE hike by February to 4.25%, then a hold and a return to 3.5% in 2028. October CPI is forecast at 3.7% y/y.

Japan: BoJ October opinions were broadly positive on hikes but with more balanced debate on equity risk and consumption. Barclays keeps a December hike and a 2% terminal rate, and now has hikes in Dec-26, Mar-27 and Jul-27.

China: growth slows to 4.2% in 2027 and 4.0% in 2028. Exports rose 35.2% y/y in October (22.7% YTD), with AI-related and green-tech goods at about 40% of exports and over 90% of YTD export growth. Property investment is expected to fall another 20% in 2027 and policy support to stay incremental.

Emerging Asia: Barclays expects hikes from RBI (to 6.00%), BSP (50bp in December to 6.00%), BoK (25bp in November and February to 3.50%), BNM (March 2027) and CBC (a closer call, 12.5bp in December). It now expects BI hikes around mid-2027, no BoT move, and MAS easing in October 2027.

EEMEA: energy shock impact has been contained so far, but food inflation is unusually weak in Czechia, Poland and Hungary, and a rebound poses upside inflation risk. Barclays sees upside risk to its dovish policy rate forecasts from Fed hikes and lingering inflation.

LatAm: Brazil's BCB paused at a 13.75% Selic after five cuts, Banxico cut 25bp to 6.25% in a 3-2 vote and signalled an extended hold, Peru hiked 25bp to 4.50%, and Colombia's new government submitted a fiscal consolidation bill worth 2.35% of GDP in 2027.

Geopolitical calendar: APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, with a possible Xi-Trump meeting and a Trump-Putin-Xi meeting. Barclays expects limited deliverables. The US-China trade truce expires on 10 January 2027.

sector_views.rationale: AI capex supports GDP and Asian exports, but its US GDP contribution is expected to fade from about 1.0pp in 2026 to 0.2pp in 2028. AI-related electronics costs are also feeding US core goods inflation.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reports earnings next week and Barclays flags it as a fresh test for the broader AI cycle amid scrutiny of the company's corporate governance. No figures or estimates are given.

risk_factors: Failure of energy prices (oil, refined products, gas) to normalise could add a Q1 2027 ECB hike.
Risks to the US rate path are skewed to the upside given rent re-acceleration and renewed core goods pressure from planned Section 301 tariffs.
A Nvidia earnings disappointment or governance issues could reverberate across the AI complex.
Brazil fiscal credibility, with a risk of higher rates if consolidation is resisted.
French fiscal and political uncertainty ahead of the 2027 elections and rising government borrowing costs.
Food inflation rebound in Eastern Europe, El Nino pressure on agricultural prices and Fed hikes as risks to EEMEA easing.
Weak labour markets and AI-driven job displacement risk in Emerging Asia and the UK.
charts_described: US core CPI Figure 1 shows broad-based firmness across three consecutive prints, with contributions from used cars, new cars, other goods, rent/OER and other services.
Figure 4 in the global synthesis shows market-implied probability of an ECB and Fed hike at the next meeting on 30 Oct, 6 Nov and 13 Nov, with hike odds rising on the latest date.
Emerging Asia Figure 2 plots DDR5 16Gb DRAM spot and contract prices, with an unusually wide spot premium that Barclays says remained resilient after the US midterms.
vol_and_positioning: Market-implied hike probability for the December FOMC moved to a full hike with an 11% chance of 50bp after the CPI print.
ECB December hike probability rose to 95% from 78% a week earlier.
geopolitical: US-Iran war in its ninth month, with Trump signalling both reduced appetite for renewed strikes and no need for a deal. Iranian demands include frozen asset release, sanctions relief and reparations.
Strait of Hormuz energy shipments remain constrained, keeping oil and gas prices elevated.
Resumption of US-Russia-Ukraine trilateral talks with calls for greater European involvement, and a possible Trump-Putin-Xi meeting at APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November.
Possible Xi-Trump meeting at APEC. The US-China trade truce expires on 10 January 2027 and rare earth exports and AI dialogue are on the agenda.
Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia hitting airports, financial districts and oil infrastructure, with risk to the East-West pipeline and Bab el-Mandeb.
Elections ahead: Spain on 29 November, French presidential election on 18 April and 2 May 2027, Argentina presidential election on 24 October 2027, and Turkiye timing debate.

tension_points.bull_case: Waller backed a December hike regardless of data and floated 50bp if core CPI printed around 0.3% m/m, and October core CPI printed 0.30%.
tension_points.bear_case: A 50bp move would signal the Fed is behind the curve and that October's hold was a mistake. Hammack declined to endorse it and other speakers stuck to a 25bp cadence.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Barclays sees the December 9 decision locked before November CPI is released on December 10, so only a very strong November payroll report could justify a jumbo move.

tension_points.bull_case: Trump signalled renewed strikes are highly unlikely, Brent fell below $90/bbl and Middle East flows are about 85% of pre-war levels.
tension_points.bear_case: A final deal looks elusive given Iranian demands, inventories are depleted and Trump said a deal is not needed, so oil stays well above pre-war levels.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Without a durable resolution of the conflict, the information set stays tilted toward central bank hikes.

tension_points.bull_case: Nasdaq 100 rebounded about 5% on robust fundamentals and strong tech earnings, and Asian equipment orders remain strong into 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Nvidia governance scrutiny, US midterm data center policy risk and a fading AI capex contribution to US GDP (1.0pp to 0.2pp by 2028).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Signs of faltering fundamentals in Nvidia's earnings next week.
